public_rationale: The claim is that code written by vibe-coding tools is hard to maintain. OX Security's October 2025 analysis of over 300 repositories found maintainability anti-patterns in 80–90% of AI-generated code. These included avoiding refactors, which builds technical debt, and over-specification, which produces fragmented systems that are hard to maintain. InfoQ reported the same findings as a new wave of technical debt. One counterpoint is a July 2025 controlled experiment that found no maintainability penalty. But its participants were mostly professional developers co-writing one feature with AI help, not amateurs letting the tool write the code. On the plain reading, the claim is supported for 2025, with the caveat that the strongest evidence is vendor research on AI code in general.
limitations: The strongest supporting evidence comes from a security vendor and is reported second-hand. The primary report could not be read.
The studies cover AI-assisted code broadly, not specifically amateur vibe coding.
Controlled experimental evidence points the other way for professional, human-supervised AI use.

statement.excerpt: And that the code they wrote would be hard to maintain?

our_interpretation: Read as an observation that, by the time of the post, code generated by vibe-coding and LLM tools had shown itself to be harder to maintain than ordinary well-engineered code.
Target period is February 2025 to October 2025 (the post month). Studies of AI-generated code from that period count.
Evidence on AI-generated code in general is accepted as relevant, because few studies isolate amateur vibe coding.
criteria.support_condition: Studies or credible analyses from 2025 find maintainability problems in AI-generated code, such as duplication, lack of refactoring, fragmentation or technical debt.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Studies from 2025 find that AI-generated code is as easy or easier to maintain than comparable human-written code.

evidence.excerpt: Over-specification (80–90%) – AI tools create narrow solutions that cannot be reused. Each variation requires new code instead of small adjustments, producing fragmented systems that are hard to maintain.
evidence.publisher: Help Net Security (reporting OX Security research)
evidence.explanation: OX's analysis of 300+ repositories found an anti-pattern producing hard-to-maintain systems in 80–90% of AI-generated code.

evidence.excerpt: Avoidance of refactors (80–90%) – Unlike experienced developers who refine and improve code, AI stops at “good enough.” It does not restructure or optimize, leading to growing technical debt.
evidence.publisher: Help Net Security (reporting OX Security research)
evidence.explanation: OX found that most AI-generated code avoids refactoring, which builds up technical debt.

evidence.excerpt: AI-generated code is “highly functional but systematically lacking in architectural judgment”, a new report from Ox Security has found.
evidence.explanation: Independent coverage of the same report, framed as a new wave of technical debt.

evidence.excerpt: Moreover, we did not observe warning signs of degraded code-level maintainability.
evidence.explanation: A controlled experiment found no maintainability penalty. But 95% of participants were professional developers co-writing one feature with AI help, which is a different practice from amateur vibe coding.
